passages.text: To know one's faults but not to correct them, to receive admonition but only to plunge deeper,--this is obstinacy.
passages.note: Admitting faults yet refusing to change

passages.text: There was once a man who was so afraid of his shadow and so disliked his own footsteps that he determined to run away from them. But the oftener he raised his feet the more footsteps he made, and though he ran very hard his shadow never left him. From this he inferred that he went too slowly, and ran as hard as he could without resting, the consequence being that his strength broke down and he died. He was not aware that by going into the shade he would have got rid of his shadow, and that by keeping still he would have put an end to his footsteps. Fool that he was!
passages.note: Running from oneself; anxiety eased by stillness

passages.text: Reverently care for your body. Carefully preserve your natural purity. Leave externals to others. Then you will not be involved. But as it is, instead of improving yourself you are trying to improve other people. Surely this is dealing with the external.
passages.note: Improve yourself rather than trying to fix others

passages.text: Real mourning grieves in silence. Real anger awes without expression. Real friendship is unison without the aid of smiles.
passages.note: Genuine feeling versus outward show; grief, anger, friendship
